questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has A(0, 0), B(2a, 0), and C(2b, 2c), with a > 0 and c ≠ 0. D is the midpoint of AC and E is the midpoint of BC. Prove that DE ∥ AB and DE = ½AB.
questions.prompt_markup: Triangle ABC has A(0, 0), B(2a, 0), and C(2b, 2c), with a > 0 and c ≠ 0. D is the midpoint of AC and E is the midpoint of BC. Prove that DE ∥ AB and DE = ½AB.
questions.correct_answer: D(b, c), E(a + b, c); DE is horizontal like AB, and DE = a = ½(2a) = ½AB.
questions.required_method: Find D and E with the midpoint formula, then compare slopes and lengths.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: both midpoints; DE has slope 0 (same y) and AB has slope 0, so DE ∥ AB (and DE ≠ AB since c ≠ 0); DE = |a + b - b| = a and AB = 2a. Invalid: checking one numerical triangle only.

questions.prompt_markup: In triangle ABC, D is the midpoint of AC and E is the midpoint of BC. Extend DE past E to F so that EF = DE. Prove that DE ∥ AB and DE = ½AB.
questions.required_method: Prove △DEC ≅ △FEB (SAS), deduce BF = DC = AD and BF ∥ AD, so ABFD is a parallelogram; then use its opposite sides.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: CE = BE, DE = FE, vertical angles at E, so △DEC ≅ △FEB (SAS); BF = DC = AD; ∠DCE ≅ ∠FBE gives BF ∥ AC (alternate interior converse); one pair of opposite sides of ABFD is parallel and congruent, so ABFD is a parallelogram; so DF ∥ AB and DF = AB; DE = ½DF = ½AB.

questions.prompt_markup: Triangle ABC has vertices A(0, 0), B(8, 0), C(2, 6). Find the vertices of its midsegment triangle and verify the ratio of areas.
questions.correct_answer: (4, 0), (5, 3), (1, 3); area of ABC = 24 and area of the midsegment triangle = 6, a ratio of 1 : 4.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the three midpoints and both areas.
questions.set_target: Prove that the segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half as long
questions.target_skill: Midsegment triangles: similarity, scale factor, and area
